cues.en: A key concept in tokenization is that tokenization is compression.
cues.zh: 斷詞的一個關鍵概念是，斷詞也是壓縮。

cues.en: Every time you tokenize text, you are also compressing that text.
cues.zh: 每次對文字斷詞，也同時壓縮了文字。

cues.en: Now, some tokenizers compress more than others, and some texts can be compressed than others.
cues.zh: 有些 tokenizer 比其他的更能壓縮，有些文字也比較容易壓縮。

cues.en: But one of the goals of tokenization is to represent text using fewer data points, which allows the
cues.zh: 但斷詞的目標之一，是用較少資料點表示文字，讓

cues.en: models to have a longer context window, which means they can perform better by integrating more information over a longer period of time.
cues.zh: 模型有更長的上下文視窗，整合更長範圍的更多資訊，提升表現。

cues.en: Now, everything that I just said is mostly sort of kind of true, but it is not trivially the case, as you will learn over the next several videos.
cues.zh: 剛才這些話，大致可以說是對的，但並非必然；接下來幾支影片就會學到。

cues.en: models to learn, process, extract meaning from, classify, and generate.
cues.zh: 模型學習、處理、擷取意義、分類與生成。

cues.en: However, there are lots of redundancies in written languages, and so therefore compression often happens as a byproduct.
cues.zh: 但書面語言有許多冗餘，因此壓縮經常是附帶結果。

cues.en: But this is a really fantastic byproduct because the more we can compress text without losing its meaning, the more text a model can process at the same time.
cues.zh: 這是很棒的附帶結果，因為能在不損失意義下壓縮越多，模型同時就能處理越多文字。

cues.en: On the other hand, there are situations where one character actually requires more than one token, and you will see examples of this with emojis.
cues.zh: 另一方面，有些情況，一個字元其實需要多個 token，表情符號就有這類例子。

cues.en: So some emojis require two tokens to represent.
cues.zh: 有些表情符號，需要兩個 token 表示。

cues.en: And you will also see an example of this in a real human language.
cues.zh: 你也會在真正的人類語言中，看到這種情況，

cues.en: In the next video.
cues.zh: 就在下一支影片。
